opex.name: Fulfillment
opex.note: Running the warehouses and delivering packages — the biggest single running cost.

opex.name: Technology & infrastructure
opex.note: Servers, data centers, and the engineers who build and run the products.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Amazon's products and winning customers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back office — finance, legal and management.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Small net charges that do not fit the other lines.

oneTimers: A $0.1B pre-tax paper loss on Amazon's common-stock investment in Rivian Automotive sits inside non-operating income — it is a revaluation of shares Amazon owns, not money lost to customers. A year ago the same line held a $2.3B loss.
otherDetail: Interest income $901M, less $713M interest expense, plus $289M of other income, net — the non-operating lines include a $0.1B pre-tax valuation loss on Amazon's stake in Rivian.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and ads in North America — the biggest piece, and it earned a $6.5B operating profit, swinging from a $0.2B loss a year ago.

segments.name: International
segments.note: The same businesses outside North America — its operating loss narrowed to $0.4B from $2.2B a year earlier.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Cloud computing rented to other companies — grew 13%, and its $7.2B operating profit was 54% of Amazon's total.

takeaways.text: North America earned a $6.5B operating profit, versus a $0.2B loss in the holiday quarter a year ago, and International's loss narrowed to $0.4B from $2.2B — the store networks' efficiency push showed up all at once.
takeaways.title: North America swung to a big profit

takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 13% to $24.2B — a $97B annual revenue run rate — and the segment earned $7.2B of operating profit, 54% of Amazon's total, up from $5.2B a year ago.
takeaways.title: AWS kept compounding

takeaways.text: Free cash flow over the trailing twelve months was a $36.8B inflow, versus an $11.6B outflow a year earlier, and net income rose to $10.6B from just $0.3B in the year-ago quarter.
takeaways.title: Free cash flow flipped sign

verdict: Amazon's holiday quarter delivered: sales rose 14% to $170.0B and operating income jumped to $13.2B from $2.7B a year ago as North America swung from a small loss to a $6.5B profit — and it kept $10.6B as profit.
